A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GradFix research, with matching titles, authors, and core experiments. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original CLIP and T5 transport experiments, masking and subset-selection ablations, and additional vision results in its appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds model-merging experiments, randomized-vector and magnitude-based controls, and ImageNet-R generalization results.

M1.justification: Equations (4)–(5) and Algorithm 1 change from retaining coordinates aligned with the gradient and subtracting them to retaining coordinates aligned with the negative gradient and adding them. With the gradient and source vector defined identically, this changes which coordinates survive, not merely notation. Section 5.2 also introduces merging pipelines with a multi-task consensus-sign mask. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The original five vision and five language benchmarks remain. V3 adds multi-task transport and transport from five independently pre-trained sources, extending the evaluated scenarios beyond single-source, single-task transfer. Appendix C.4 additionally evaluates held-out ImageNet-R generalization.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates TIES-Merging alongside Task Arithmetic in the new merging comparisons; TIES was only cited in v1. It also adds magnitude-scaled masking and a randomized source-task-vector comparator, distinct from the existing random-sign mask. The original single-task comparators, including TransFusion, remain.

E3.justification: V3 introduces protocols comparing masking before versus after merging, five-source aggregation, random vectors matched to source-vector statistics, and paired downstream/ImageNet-R testing. These substantially expand the evaluation design. The original training budgets, per-class supervision budgets, optimizer settings, and validation-based scaling selection are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test magnitude information in masking, whether source-task structure is necessary, which merging order works in each setting, and whether transport preserves held-out generalization. The existing subset-selection study moves largely to Appendix C.2; the scaling sensitivity and layerwise sign-agreement analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over random seeds, standard deviations in Tables 5–6, and uncertainty bands for random subset selection. V3 adds no explicit run counts, seed lists, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures; the retained tables' uncertainty values are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 retain their numerical results. Substantial new results include multi-task TIES accuracy of 66.02 with Merge-then-Mask versus 54.67 without GradFix, and randomized-vector accuracy of 54.79 versus GradFix's 64.45 at one example per class. Table 8 adds ImageNet-R accuracies of 79.27–80.17 versus the target's 79.78 zero-shot baseline. These are newly reported comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Section 4 substantively corrects the central mathematical account: the Taylor expansion removes duplicated scaling, the inner-product derivation matches the revised update, and Equation (10) bounds estimated-sign agreement with the negative true gradient instead of v1's gradient/oracle-task-vector event. Appendix A is aligned with this formulation. Appendix F also adds an analytical computational-cost derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add improved multi-task and multi-source model merging as an explicit contribution, extending the paper's main claim beyond individual task-vector transport. The existing claims about few-shot transfer, avoiding additional fine-tuning, and first-order descent remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations connecting magnitude-mask failure to basin-specific scales, randomized-vector failure to missing source knowledge, and merging-order effects to complementary or misaligned coordinates. It also interprets ImageNet-R results as preserving general robustness. That last interpretation is stronger than some displayed results, including the DTD support-accuracy decrease from 79.78 to 79.27.

D1.justification: V3 adds an explicit code-repository link beyond v1's supplementary-code statement and documents operation-level FLOP assumptions in Appendix F. Table 5 corrects the ViT-B/16 target-checkpoint identifier to match the main text already present in v1. The original hyperparameter values and one-step fine-tuning description are retained; no measured runtime or detailed hardware specification is added.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to Gargiulo et al. (2025), Hendrycks et al. (2020), Kaplan et al. (2020), and Porrello et al. (2026), while removing Zhou et al. (2024) and Zeng et al. (2024). The central positioning relative to model merging, rebasing, and gradient-sign methods remains similar. Bibliographic metadata changes do not constitute additional research-positioning changes.

P1.justification: V3 extensively revises explanatory prose across the abstract, introduction, method, and experimental discussion, consistently distinguishing gradients from negative gradients. It also reorganizes the experimental narrative, moves detailed subset selection to the appendix, and separates additional results, ablations, datasets, hyperparameters, and computational analysis into dedicated appendix sections.

P2.justification: V3 adds substantial tables for merging, randomized-vector controls, and paired task/support performance, and expands the masking table. It relocates the subset-selection figure to the appendix, regroups the supplementary tables, and redraws the scaling-sensitivity plot with revised markers and axis ticks. The masking illustration and heatmap values are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves important sign, scaling, and estimator-statement inconsistencies in the central method and theory, while adding meaningful controls and merging/generalization tests that address validation gaps in v1. These substantially improve mathematical coherence and empirical support. Qualifications remain: unchanged legacy scores do not establish reruns of the revised algorithm, the ImageNet-R preservation claim overstates some results, and computational savings are approximate analytical estimates. These limitations do not outweigh the documented gains.
